newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arboyne to raise up to US$20 million.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arboyne to raise up to US$20 million.

text.p: Australian miner Arboyne NL said on Thursday it plans to raise up to US$20 million through a convertible note issue to help fund development of the Nonoc nickel project in the Philippines.
Arboyne said it would seek shareholder approval to make the interest free issue at a conversion price of US$0.25 per share.
"The issue is a key plank in the ongoing preparations to refurbish the Nonoc nickel complex in the Philippines," it said.
The company said the capital raising would be used to fund pre-refurbishment work on the Nonoc mine and refinery, which it has said will cost about US$370 million.
"This early pre-refurbishment work will be done ahead of a planned public capital raising, scheduled for later in the year," the company said in a statement.
Chief executive Steve Kesler said the capital raising was an important and timely step in the redevelopment of Nonoc.
"The project is now well advanced and the additional funds will allow Arboyne and Pacific Nickel to maintain momentum," he said.
Arboyne secured an option to acquire Nonoc last July through Pacific Nickel which has the rights to acquire the complex.
The Nonoc nickel refining complex is capable of producing 65 pounds of metal a year and was one of the world's biggest nickel refineries before it closed in 1986.

Kesler said that subject to shareholder approval, Kvaemer Plc group had agreed to increase its investment in Arboyne by subscribing for a minimum US$5 million of convertible notes - subject to an equal contribution from other parties - and reserved the right to subscribe for a further US$5 million.
